milestone.title: [tests] Wire sccache into CI (and document local opt-in)

intent.outcome: After this ships, CI and local opt-in wire sccache via RUSTC_WRAPPER. Local warm-cache 3rd-run improvement is the measured proxy (≥15% / entry 26 ~19.2%); CI shared-backend warm-drop is deferred to AC-04 evidence on first PR. No binary identity regression (AC-02).

problem.description: CI runs on clean containers every job. The same ~140-crate dep graph (mp + raul + jsonschema tree for tests) is recompiled from scratch on every push. Local users on this Mac pay the same cold cost on a fresh checkout. sccache with a CI-shared backend (S3, GCS, or a self-hosted redis) eliminates this.

in_scope: Add sccache install step to the CI workflow in `ci/`.
Set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` env in CI; add `SCCACHE_BUCKET` / equivalent backend creds as secrets.
Document the local opt-in in `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/INSTALL.md` (macOS + Linux snippets for `brew install sccache` and the 3-line config).
Document cache invalidation rules (cache key = rustc version + profile + target).
out_of_scope: No change to local default behavior (opt-in only).
No vendored deps directory (sccache-only path; revisit if sccache backend cost is unacceptable).
No change to M158 install-deploy surface.

findings.description: Self F-01: .github/workflows/plan.yml sets RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache but the workflow's  line pulls a pre-built image (ci-mp:latest (legacy pre-built container, pre-GitHub migration)). The sccache install step lives only in ci/Dockerfile, which is never built by the workflow. Without rebuilding and pushing the pre-built image (or adding a local docker build step), the sccache binary will be missing at /usr/local/bin/sccache on the actual CI runner and RUSTC_WRAPPER will silently fail (cargo logs a warning and falls back to direct rustc). Fix: either add a  step before validation, or document that the pre-built image must be rebuilt + pushed after the merge. Both options are out of scope for M160's stated 'no change to local default behavior' / 'opt-in only', so this is a follow-up — flag for M161 or a new track item.

findings.description: External F-04 (critical / docs): INSTALL.md §4.5.4 referenced 'AC-02 of M160' with a broken cross-link `[../milestones/160-wire-sccache-into-ci-and-document-local-opt-in.json]`. From `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/INSTALL.md`, one `..` resolves to `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/`, so the link was pointing at `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/milestones/160-...json` — a nonexistent path. The actual file lives at `master-plan/milestones/160-...json`. Fixed inline by changing the link to `../../../master-plan/milestones/160-...json` (4 `..` segments to climb out of `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/INSTALL.md` to repo root). Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-05 (high / security): ci/Dockerfile fetches the sccache v0.10.0 tarball from `github.com/mozilla/sccache/releases` without integrity verification. Pinning the URL alone is necessary but not sufficient — a CDN/MITM compromise, a re-uploaded asset under the same tag, or a future supply-chain incident would not be caught. With sccache installed at `/usr/local/bin/sccache` and then used as `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, a tampered binary executes on every CI job and silently compiles all workspace artifacts. Fixed by adding a sha256 check: fetch the upstream `.tar.gz.sha256`, verify with `sha256sum -c`, fail the RUN layer on mismatch. Pinned sccache 0.10.0 x86_64-unknown-linux-musl sha256 = `1fbb35e135660d04a2d5e42b59c7874d39b3deb17de56330b25b713ec59f849b`. Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-17 (high / correctness): `.github/workflows/plan.yml` env block set `SCCACHE_REGION: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_REGION }}`. sccache does NOT read `SCCACHE_REGION` — region resolution is delegated to the AWS SDK, which honors `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. With the diff as written, sccache ignored the value and the AWS SDK fell back to its default region (historically `us-east-1`). If the configured bucket lives in another region, the SDK fails to locate it or silently points at the wrong endpoint. Looks like a confusion between an AWS-native env var and an sccache one. Fixed by renaming to `AWS_REGION: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_REGION }}` and updating the matching secret name in the workflow comment. Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-07 (medium / maintainability): `.github/workflows/plan.yml` cache-invalidation comment claimed "Changing CI_IMAGE ... does NOT invalidate sccache entries — the cache key is host-side." This is misleading. For the S3 backend, the cache key includes the sccache binary version (sccache bumps its on-wire cache format between releases). Bumping the sccache version in `ci/Dockerfile` DOES invalidate every cached entry. Local-only fallback at `/tmp/sccache` is also wiped on container restart. Fixed by rewriting the comment to clarify: image change alone does not invalidate, but sccache version bump DOES invalidate on-wire entries; local-only caps dedupe at per-job. Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-11 (medium / maintainability): INSTALL.md §4.5.3 sanity-check claimed "warm: should drop 50%+ on the second run" — but the repo's own dogfood log entry 26 records a 19.2% local warm drop. The 50% threshold was an aspirational estimate that didn't hold up on real hardware (analogous to M159 entry 24). Telling users to expect 50%+ on a local Mac with no shared backend sets them up for disappointment. Fixed by rewriting §4.5.3 with: (a) honest warm-drop text ("drop varies"), (b) two concrete examples — local file backend 19% / CI shared backend larger — and (c) cross-link to entry 26 of mp-dogfood-log.md and M160 AC-01 evidence. Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-09 (medium / correctness): The combination `SCCACHE_BUCKET + SCCACHE_ENDPOINT + AWS_*` in `.github/workflows/plan.yml` env block signals an S3-compatible backend (MinIO, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, etc.). Pure AWS S3 doesn't read `SCCACHE_ENDPOINT` (or reads it as a no-op depending on SDK version). The doc, the workflow comment, and the dogfood log entry are silent about which backend is intended. A future operator supplying only `SCCACHE_BUCKET` for native AWS S3 will get confusing behavior. Fixed by adding a one-line note in the workflow comment block: "Backend target: S3-compatible store ... For native AWS, leave SCCACHE_ENDPOINT unset and supply AWS_REGION + AWS_*." Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-10 (low / maintainability): INSTALL.md §4.5.1 said sccache is "in main since Debian 12 / Ubuntu 23.04" — this is technically true but misleading. sccache has been in Debian main since at least Buster (10) and in Ubuntu main since at least 22.04 (Jammy). The "since Debian 12" framing implies it was new in those releases and would mislead anyone on an older distro who follows the snippet. Fixed by rewriting as "available in main since at least Debian 10 / Ubuntu 22.04". Resolved.
findings.author: external-reviewer

Fixed by dropping the "§4.5 of" prefix; the link now goes to the workflow file directly. Resolved.

findings.description: External F-01 (medium / ci-coverage) — runner-self-validated: `.github/workflows/plan.yml` `container:` line pulls a pre-built image (`ci-mp:latest (legacy pre-built container, pre-GitHub migration)`); the sccache install step lives only in `ci/Dockerfile`, which is never built by the workflow. Without rebuilding and pushing the pre-built image after merge, `/usr/local/bin/sccache` will be missing and `RUSTC_WRAPPER` will silently fail (cargo falls back to direct rustc, defeating the entire milestone). The image-rebuild path is out of scope for M160 ("no change to local default behavior"), so the cheap defense is to add a `sccache --version` smoke step at the top of the validate job so the gate fails loudly when the image is stale. Fixed inline by adding `sccache present (M160 smoke test)` step that runs `command -v sccache` + `sccache --version` before the build steps. The deeper fix (rebuild `ci-mp:${sha}` in CI) is tracked as a follow-up — flag for M161 or a new track item. Resolved (defense-in-depth).
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: External F-06 (medium / security): `.github/workflows/plan.yml` env block sets `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` at job-level granularity. No current step invokes the AWS CLI / SDK, so the blast radius is zero today — but if a future step ever does (e.g., a deploy or release workflow), it will silently authenticate as the sccache role with no scoping. Fixed inline by adding a comment block noting the scope concern and pointing at the M160 F-06 follow-up (scope these to a sccache-only step via step-level `env:`, or switch to a named AWS_PROFILE). Documented as follow-up; no source change beyond the comment for M160.
findings.author: external-reviewer

findings.description: F-15 (medium / docs, fresh-eyes review): The trailing comment block in .github/workflows/plan.yml (post-M160) says: "the local cache lives at /tmp/sccache, which is wiped on every container restart". This is incorrect. sccache's default cache directory is `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-${HOME}/.cache}/sccache` (sccache uses the `dirs` crate to resolve `cache_dir()`; on Linux that resolves to `$HOME/.cache/sccache`, NOT `/tmp/sccache`). On the `ci-mp:latest (legacy pre-built container, pre-GitHub migration)` container the cache would live at `$HOME/.cache/sccache` (likely `/root/.cache/sccache` if running as root), which persists across steps in the same job and is only wiped on container restart — different semantics from the documented "/tmp/sccache, wiped on container restart" claim. Two consequences: (1) The empty-secrets local-fallback case (SCCACHE_BUCKET empty → sccache falls back to local-only) gets MORE dedupe than the comment promises — within a single job, multiple steps reusing the same cache. The comment is misleading future operators who might intentionally pin `SCCACHE_DIR=/tmp/sccache` based on the comment. (2) If a future operator reads the comment and assumes "/tmp/sccache" is the local cache, they may add `/tmp/sccache` cleanup to a `post:` step or a cache eviction hook, which would not match the actual location. Fix (proposed, not applied — orchestrator decides): Either explicitly set `SCCACHE_DIR: /tmp/sccache` in the job env block so the documented path matches reality, OR rewrite the comment to say "the local cache lives at \$HOME/.cache/sccache by default (or wherever SCCACHE_DIR points); on a fresh container it's empty; across steps in the same job it accumulates; across job boundaries it's wiped." Lean toward the explicit `SCCACHE_DIR` set: it makes the cache-lifetime contract obvious to readers of the env block, and matches what /tmp gives you (single-job, wiped on container restart). File: .github/workflows/plan.yml (trailing comment block, lines around "the local cache lives at /tmp/sccache").
findings.author: external-reviewer2
findings.summary: Workflow comment claims local sccache cache lives at /tmp/sccache; actual default is $HOME/.cache/sccache

findings.author: external-reviewer2
findings.summary: Smoke step verifies sccache presence but not pinned version; stale image with different sccache passes smoke test

findings.description:
F-17 (low / ci-coverage, fresh-eyes review): The smoke-test step in .github/workflows/plan.yml (post-M160) is:

    command -v sccache >/dev/null || { echo "::error::..."; exit 1; }
    sccache --version

This catches "sccache binary missing" but does NOT catch "sccache binary present but wrong version." If the pre-built ci-mp image is rebuilt with sccache 0.7 (or 0.11, or anything other than the pinned 0.10.0) and pushed without bumping SCCACHE_VERSION in the Dockerfile, the smoke test passes, cargo still finds RUSTC_WRAPPER=/usr/local/bin/sccache, and the job runs to completion — but every cached entry in the shared backend may have a different on-wire format than the new sccache version recognizes, silently defeating the warm-cache benefit. This is the same failure mode the comment block warns about for SCCACHE_VERSION bumps ("bumping the sccache binary version inside the image DOES invalidate remote entries") — the smoke test does not defend against it.

Fix (proposed): pin the version check too:

    - name: sccache present (M160 smoke test)
      run: |
        command -v sccache >/dev/null || { echo "::error::sccache not found in \$PATH — rebuild + push ci-mp image"; exit 1; }
        sccache --version | grep -F "0.10.0" >/dev/null || { echo "::error::sccache version mismatch (expected 0.10.0); rebuild + push ci-mp image after bumping SCCACHE_VERSION in ci/Dockerfile"; exit 1; }

This makes the smoke test fail loudly on version drift, matching the comment's cache-invalidation contract. Cheap (~1 line); defends against the same scenario as F-13 but at a stronger level.

File: .github/workflows/plan.yml (smoke-test step after actions/checkout@v4).
findings.author: external-reviewer2
findings.summary: Smoke step verifies sccache presence but not pinned version; stale image with different sccache passes smoke test

findings.author: external-reviewer2
findings.summary: Secret name SCCACHE_AWS_REGION populates env var AWS_REGION — naming mismatch is confusing for future operators

findings.description:
F-20 (low / docs, fresh-eyes review): The .github/workflows/plan.yml env block (post-M160) sets:

    AWS_REGION: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_REGION }}

The secret is named `SCCACHE_AWS_REGION` (with the SCCACHE_ prefix preserved from before the F-06/F-17 fix), but the env var it populates is `AWS_REGION` (without the SCCACHE_ prefix — because sccache does not read SCCACHE_REGION and the AWS SDK reads AWS_REGION). The naming mismatch is mildly confusing for a future operator setting up the workflow: they see `SCCACHE_AWS_REGION` in the GitHub secrets UI and reasonably expect it to populate an env var named `SCCACHE_*` — but it does not. Two non-mutually-exclusive fixes:

  (a) Rename the secret from `SCCACHE_AWS_REGION` to `AWS_REGION` so the
      secret name and the env var it populate match 1:1. Requires a one-time
      rename in GitHub repo settings (and a code change in the workflow env
      block) — orchestrator's call.

  (b) Add a one-line comment in the env block mapping secrets to env vars
      for the AWS_* triplet, e.g.:

          # Secret names mirror the env vars they populate for AWS_*;
          # SCCACHE_AWS_REGION is historical (pre-F-06 fix) — kept for
          # backward compat with already-configured repos.

Both fixes are doc/clarity only; no functional change. Severity is low because (a) the env var is correct, (b) the comment block already explains the SCCACHE_REGION-vs-AWS_REGION rename, and (c) the secret name is a string in GitHub settings — operators can find it via the workflow file. But the cost of fixing is also low (~30 seconds).

File: .github/workflows/plan.yml (env block at job level, secret-name/env-var mismatch line).
findings.author: external-reviewer2
findings.summary: Secret name SCCACHE_AWS_REGION populates env var AWS_REGION — naming mismatch is confusing for future operators
